Purpose and scope

One ordered source of work

This backlog converts the project vision, MVP scope slides, sprint backlog, and persona work into implementation-ready slices. Items are ordered by safety, learning value, user value, dependency, and delivery effort. Priority describes sequence; it is not permission to launch.

The five-day sprint remains the Iteration 01 baseline. Broader items—payment integration, SMS OTP, loyalty, direct PRC integration, and multi-school tooling—stay visible here without being added to that sprint.

Release gateNo real personal data or payment should enter the pilot until the privacy, safeguarding, data-flow, content-approval, and official-payment gates have written owners and evidence. Until then, test with synthetic data only.

Release strategy

Sequence risk before scale

Release labels are planning horizons, not promised dates. A release advances only when its exit gates are met.

R0 · VALIDATE

Discovery and approval

  • Confirm facts, roles, lawful basis, and payment boundary
  • Test separate sponsor and recipient journeys
  • Approve pilot scorecard and stop conditions
R1 · PILOT MVP

One-school controlled pilot

  • Education, referral, consent, intake, secure handoff
  • Protected operations and aggregate evidence
  • Synthetic data until every launch gate passes
R1.1 · ENHANCE

Improve verified friction

  • Additional languages and assisted completion
  • Renewal reminders and private recognition
  • Provider integrations only after approval
R2 · SCALE

Integrate and expand

  • Direct PRC integration if technically authorized
  • Multi-school and chapter operations
  • Expansion based on evidence, ownership, and funding

Scope reconciliation

What the sources mean for delivery

The product backlog deliberately keeps committed, gated, and deferred work separate.

Source directionBacklog treatmentWhy
Landing page, storyboard, referral QR/link, intake form, and pilot data storeP1 · R1 Pilot MVPExplicitly included in the supplied Iteration 01 scope and MVP slides.
Payment integrationP0 decision gate, then R1.1 candidateThe slides call it conditional; the sprint backlog explicitly excludes it. The MVP therefore starts with an approved official-payment handoff unless integration is authorized.
Authentication and SMS OTPAdmin authentication in R1; enrollee OTP decision-gatedProtected admin access is required for real data. SMS OTP adds cost, delivery, and privacy dependencies and is not in the five-day committed scope.
Loyalty, points, gamification, ambassador app, advanced analyticsP2/P3 · R1.1 or R2Explicitly out of Iteration 01. Any recognition must remain private and must not pressure or identify recipients.
Direct PRC backend/API integration and multi-school rolloutP3 · R2 ScaleRequires partner approval, interface specifications, operational ownership, and evidence from the controlled pilot.

Working agreements

Ready and done mean more than coded

Definition of Ready

  • User and intended outcome are explicit.
  • Acceptance checks are testable.
  • PRC-controlled wording or fields identify an approver.
  • Data classification and access impact are known.
  • Dependencies, analytics, and accessibility needs are identified.
  • Story fits the target iteration or is split.

Definition of Done

  • Acceptance checks pass on supported mobile browsers.
  • Automated tests and peer review pass.
  • Accessibility, privacy, and security checks are recorded.
  • Telemetry excludes prohibited personal data.
  • Approved copy and version are traceable.
  • Runbook, rollback, known limits, and release note are updated.

Pilot release gates

  • Named PRC approver and approved public fact sheet.
  • Approved privacy notice, lawful basis, and role map.
  • Approved payment and reconciliation route.
  • Approved data fields, retention, deletion, and incident process.
  • School/minor safeguarding requirements completed.
  • Dry run passes with synthetic data and no critical defects.

Source basis

References and assumptions

  • Safe Card Project Vision Goals and Objectives, supplied project document, reviewed 4 Sep 2026.
  • SafeCard MVP Sprint Backlog, supplied artifact.
  • SafeCard User Personas and Journey Maps, supplied artifact; persona details treated as hypotheses.
  • Supplied MVP scope slides covering the landing page, benefit storyboard, referral QR/link, intake form, pilot data store, conditional payment integration, and role-based authentication/SMS OTP.
  • Philippine Red Cross membership information and National Privacy Commission consent guidance, referenced by the project materials.

Planning note: Program terms, prices, benefits, eligibility, claims instructions, contacts, brand use, translations, and timelines may change. The backlog treats them as controlled content and requires revalidation and recorded PRC approval before any production release. Story points express relative complexity, not calendar duration.
